terms.meaning: An object that gives out its own light.
An object seen only because it reflects light from elsewhere.
Does not let light pass through.
The change in the direction of light by a mirror or shiny surface.
In a mirror image, left and right are swapped.

items.name: Proof with holes and pipes
items.formula: Light passes through holes only when they are in a line, and through a straight pipe but not a bent one.
items.example: A candle cannot be seen through a bent pipe.

items.name: Sunlight reaching the Earth
items.formula: It takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds.

items.name: Examples of non-luminous bodies
items.formula: The Moon, planets, trees and mirrors.
items.example: The Moon shines by reflecting sunlight.

items.name: What a shadow needs
items.formula: A source of light, an object that blocks light, and a screen.
items.example: A wall can be the screen for a hand held in torchlight.

items.name: How dark is a shadow?
items.formula: Opaque: dark. Translucent: lighter. Some transparent objects: faint.
items.example: Cardboard gives a darker shadow than tracing paper.

items.name: Size of a shadow
items.formula: Object nearer the light: bigger shadow. Object nearer the screen: smaller shadow.
items.example: Move your hand towards the torch and its shadow grows.

items.name: Colour of a shadow
items.formula: The colour of an opaque object does not change its shadow.
items.example: A red ball and a green ball cast the same dark shadow.

items.name: Shadow puppets of Karnataka
items.example: Andhra Pradesh has a similar form, Tholu Bommalata.

items.name: Image in a plane mirror
items.formula: Erect, the same size, cannot be caught on a screen, and laterally inverted.
items.example: Raise your right hand and your image raises its left.

items.name: Distance of the image
items.formula: As far behind the mirror as the object is in front.
items.example: An object 30 cm in front has its image 30 cm behind, so they are 60 cm apart.

items.name: Writing on an ambulance
items.formula: The word is printed reversed, so a driver in front reads it correctly in a mirror.
items.example: Letters such as A, H and M look the same in a mirror.

items.name: Aranmula Kannadi
items.formula: A handmade mirror of polished metal alloy from Kerala.
items.example: It has no glass in it.

items.name: Pinhole camera
items.formula: Gives an inverted image on a screen, with the object’s colours.
items.example: A building appears upside down on the tracing paper.

items.name: Periscope
items.formula: Two parallel plane mirrors in a Z-shaped tube, for seeing over obstacles.

items.name: Kaleidoscope
items.formula: Three mirror strips joined as a triangle. Many reflections make patterns.
items.example: Coloured bangle pieces make new designs when it is turned.

mistakes.text: The Moon is not luminous. It only reflects sunlight.
A plane mirror image is laterally inverted but upright. A pinhole camera image is upside down.
A shadow does not show the object’s colour. An image in a pinhole camera does.
